newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower for fifth straight session.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower for fifth straight session.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed lower for the fifth consecutive session on Monday as a consolidation following the market's recent steep rises deepened, brokers said.
They said many investors remained firmly on the sidelines, sharply reducing the trading volume.
Kia Motors rebounded on the hope the state-run Korea Development Bank would soon grant it fresh loans.
The composite stock index lost 7.35 points to 753.05 with more than three times as many losers as gainers at 611 to 191. Volume fell to 31.77 million shares from 42.12 million last Friday.
"The sharply reduced volume mirrors chilled investor sentiment," said Park Key-pyong at Hanyang Securities. "The consolidation is expected to continue until the beginning of July."
A trader at Citicorp International Securities was more gloomy as he forecast the market would not rebound until August when it would rise to the 850 level.
"We almost cleared our positions as we believe economic recovery looked to take more time," he said.
Brokers said expected margin loan calls among smaller-cap shares also pressured the market.
Korea Development Bank said Kia Motors and Kia Steel each asked the bank for 30 billion won in loans. The bank said it was reviewing the request.
Brokers said many investors believed the government would intervene, if Kia faced some financial problems.
Securities houses came into the spotlight as the government would allow them to issue corporate bonds from next month. The securities sub-index rose 6.93 points to 1,371.44.
Banking shares were in demand after a local newspaper reported the government would expand the individual ownership ceiling in banks to 15 percent from the current four percent.

Chohung Bank was the most actively traded stock with 1.03 million shares changing hands. It gained 60 won to 6,010. Korea Exchange Bank rose 90 won to 6,380 with the third largest trading volume of 769,480 shares.
All four IPO shares ended their first day of trading at their upper limits, the Korea Stock Exchange said.
Pusan City Gas Co Ltd gained 2,600 won to 35,100 and the bourse statement said 630,060 shares remained unmatched even though investors wanted to buy the new shares at upper-limit prices.
